status: measured and recorded. No published number changes. One prior MEASUREMENT is downgraded to a derivation -- the tangent dimension 7 was never a measurement -- and one new instrument defect is recorded against a module written specifically to avoid it.
subject: src/aionq/majorana.py, the coordinate-free form of the free-fermion certificate, against src/aionq/matchgate_defect.py and src/aionq/transport_fiber.py
the_criticism_that_prompted_it: the repository owner observed that these instruments use indices rather than tensor fields or invariant structures. The criticism is correct and specific: `_OFF_BLOCK` is a literal list of eight matrix positions, `is_matchgate_matrix` slices rows {0,3} and {1,2}, and the whole module is hard-wired to 4x4 and cannot be asked about three qubits.

parity.index_form: sum of |U[r,c]|^2 over eight listed positions
parity.invariant_form: ||U-||_F where U+- = (U +- P U P)/2 and P = Z^(x)n is the fermionic parity
parity.agreement: exactly equal, difference 0.0, on every gate of the test zoo. The eight forbidden entries ARE the coordinates of the parity-odd part; the index version was computing a Z2 grading without saying so.

matchgate_condition.index_form: two tests -- parity block structure, then |det A - det B|
matchgate_condition.invariant_form: one test -- U c_k U* stays in span{c_1..c_2n} for the Jordan-Wigner Majorana modes
matchgate_condition.what_the_unification_shows: CZ preserves the Z2 grading, so its parity defect is 0 and the index version requires a SECOND, separate determinant test to reject it. The covariant condition rejects it in the one number, because preserving the grading is not preserving the Majorana span.

measurement_1_the_index_lists_were_shado.generalisation: the index test is 2-qubit only. The covariant test is written for any n and was run at n = 3.

measurement_2_the_aggregator_was_still_r.what_happened: the first covariant implementation took `max` over the individual Majorana residuals. Its FORMULA has no indices. Its REDUCTION does: a maximum over a basis is not invariant under rotating the basis.

measured.max_aggregator: deviation 1.24e-01 under 80 random O(4) Majorana frames, 1.26e-01 under Gaussian conjugation

measurement_2_the_aggregator_was_still_r.why_sum_of_squares_is_the_right_one: sum_k ||(1-Pi) U c_k U*||^2 is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of a linear map, and composing that map with an orthogonal frame rotation does not change it. The max is a norm of a coordinate list.
measurement_2_the_aggregator_was_still_r.classification: eighth occurrence in this repository of a guard or quantity whose claim outruns its instrument, and the FIRST occurrence inside a module written specifically to be invariant. Recorded as a bound correction in self_audit.
measurement_2_the_aggregator_was_still_r.executable_form: tests/test_majorana.py::test_a_max_over_the_basis_is_not_invariant_and_a_sum_of_squares_is, which asserts BOTH that the bad aggregator misbehaves and that the shipped one does not

measurement_3_a_measurement_downgraded_t.what_R1C_reported: tangent dimension of the certified class = 7 inside 16, obtained as a numerical Jacobian rank with a nine-order singular-value gap
measurement_3_a_measurement_downgraded_t.what_it_actually_is: the Gaussian unitaries are generated by Hamiltonians quadratic in Majoranas. The quadratic monomials c_j c_k with j < k span so(2n); the identity contributes the global phase. So dim = C(2n,2) + 1 = n(2n-1) + 1, with nothing measured.
measurement_3_a_measurement_downgraded_t.confirmation: the Jacobian rank was recomputed against the covariant defining functions at n = 2 and n = 3 and returns 7 and 16, matching the algebra exactly, with singular-value gaps of 8.7e9 and 4.3e9.
measurement_3_a_measurement_downgraded_t.why_this_is_worth_recording_rather_than_: R1C presented 7 as a measurement that happened to agree with an arithmetic prediction. It is the other way round: the prediction is the fact and the rank was its coordinate shadow. An instrument that returns the answer the algebra already knows is an instrument that can be trusted where the algebra is silent -- which is the actual value of the R1C Jacobian, and it is a smaller claim than the one R1C made.

measurement_4_the_frame_group_was_miside.statement: qubit relabelling permutes Majorana PAIRS, so S_n is a finite subgroup of O(2n). The frame group of the fermionic frame bundle is O(2n), continuous, of dimension C(2n,2) = n(2n-1).
measurement_4_the_frame_group_was_miside.consequence_for_the_earlier_rounds: R1B and R1C walked AGL(1,16) inside S_16 -- 240 isolated points of a 496-dimensional Lie group. The step they measured is what a discrete subgroup of a Lie group can see. R1C already said a finite group cannot produce a dimension phenomenon; this identifies which continuous group it is a subgroup OF, which is the thing that was missing.
measurement_4_the_frame_group_was_miside.not_claimed: that walking O(2n) has been done. It has not. What is established is the containment and the dimensions.

measurement_5_the_transverse_sphere_is_n.method: 3000 unit Hermitian directions sampled at a point of the class (n = 2, codimension 9, so the transverse direction sphere is S^8); first-order escape rate recorded for each
measurement_5_the_transverse_sphere_is_n.reading: escape order is 1 in every direction (R1C) but the RATE is not constant: it varies by a factor of 4 across the transverse sphere. So the class does not sit inside a round cone, and the first-order geometry is genuinely anisotropic. This is the object a partitioning or tessellation argument would act on -- the level sets of the escape rate on S^8 -- and it is measured here for the first time.
measurement_5_the_transverse_sphere_is_n.not_claimed: any partition, any incidence bound, any consequence. An anisotropic function on a sphere is raw material.

typed_remainders.statement: gaussian_defect costs O(n * 4^n) as written, since it conjugates 2n operators of size 2^n. It was run at n = 3 and is feasible to n = 5 or 6. The free-fermion class has dimension n(2n-1)+1 inside 4^n, so codimension grows exponentially while every geometric statement here is at n <= 3. Whether uniform first-order escape survives that limit is not measured, and exponentially growing codimension is exactly the regime where transversality constants degrade.

the covariant defect subsumes the parity and determinant residuals but NOT the locality one, and that is correct rather than a gap: locality is a statement about which wires a gate sits on, it is not a property of the operator at all, and it is precisely the residual the frame group moves. The index-dependence of the code and the frame-dependence of the quantity coincide exactly -- three residuals expressible invariantly are orbit-collapsed, the one expressible only in indices is orbit-resolving.
